threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You carry an umbrella but never use it, because you still believe the weather forecast won't mislead you, bless your heart.
Saw a bloke in a full tux sitting on the 196, sipping a Red Stripe. Turns out he was coming from a wedding in Herne Hill - life in Brixton never disappoints.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a group of kids playing in a fountain on Karl-Marx-Straße, completely unfazed by the hustle around them.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find spontaneous raves in abandoned buildings, where the smell of old wood mingles with a bass drop and a crowd of strangers becomes family for a night.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they navigate BART's delays; if they just shrug and keep eating their burrito, they're a true San Franciscan.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading the bus stop with a sax. Everyone waiting silently vibing, then a kid tossed him a dollar. Classic San Francisco moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but it’s really the small plazas and local bars that make it vibrant—like the charm of Plaça del Sol at sunset.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They always ask for 'patatas bravas' to be served with ketchup instead of alioli. You can spot them a mile away!

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of just 'the train'. Also, the way you search for parking like it's an Olympic sport.
I saw a guy on the 50 bus confidently singing opera at 2am, the whole bus just went silent, then clapped when he finished. Pure Brixton magic.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I saw a guy in a tutu arguing with his dog over a kebab at the corner of Weserstraße.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Kreuzberg’s raw energy on a Monday morning during the BVG strike—everyone somehow still manages to get around by bike and foot. It's chaotic, but beautifully so.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name all the taco trucks but still complain about the new coffee shop that charges $6 for a drip.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Heard a woman arguing passionately with a pigeon at Civic Center today. Muni might be a mess, but sometimes the real drama is right on the platform.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always ask for 'tapas' but miss the incredible bocadillos at the corner bars. It's like asking for a sandwich in Paris and ignoring the croissants.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always spot a newcomer by their bewilderment at the local grocery store’s lack of peanut butter options. Classic dead giveaway.
